n: A thanksgiving that pairs with Psalm 20: the prayer has been answered. The king rejoices in the Lord’s strength and victory.

f.w: The king shall joy in thy strength

n: God has granted the king’s heart’s desire and not refused his request — an echo of Psalm 20:4.

f.w: Thou hast given him his heart's desire

n: God came to meet him with rich blessings and set a crown of pure gold on his head.

f.g: Went before, came to meet (old meaning).

n: The king asked for life, and God gave him length of days forever. For Christians this points beyond David to the eternal reign of Christ.

f.w: length of days for ever and ever

n: Through God’s help the king’s glory is great; God has given him splendor and majesty.
God has made him a blessing forever and filled him with joy in his presence.

f.g: Literally “made him blessings forever” — a source of blessing to others.

n: The king trusts in the Lord; because of the Most High’s steadfast love he will not be shaken. This is the center of the psalm.

f.w: the mercy of the most High

n: Now the people address the king (or God): your hand will find all your enemies.
When you appear, they will burn as in a blazing furnace; the Lord will swallow them up in his anger.
Their descendants will be wiped from the earth.
Though they plot evil and scheme against God, they cannot succeed.

f.w: a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform

n: God will make them turn and run when he aims his arrows at their faces.
The psalm ends in praise: be exalted, Lord, in your strength; we will sing of your power.
